group.title: Appearance and personality
sources: Words and CEFR levels chosen by the authors from general knowledge of English; meanings, examples and sentences are original

Word-list licences checked 2026-10-25: CEFR-J Wordlist 1.5 (Tono Laboratory, TUFS; free with citation, A1-B2) and NGSL/NAWL (CC BY-SA 4.0) were not copied; Oxford 3000 and English Vocabulary Profile terms were not confirmed, so they were not used

words.meaning: Very thin, often too thin.
examples: The {skinny} boy needed a smaller belt.
wrong: He was so skinny that he couldn’t fit through the door.

words.meaning: A little fat in a pleasant, round way.
examples: The baby had {plump} pink cheeks.
wrong: The plump man was very thin and bony.

words.meaning: Having large, strong muscles.
examples: The swimmer has {muscular} arms.
wrong: He was so muscular that he could not lift a cup.

words.meaning: Having a big, strong body.
examples: The {well-built} guard stood at the door.
wrong: The well-built man was small and weak.

words.meaning: Having little or no hair on the head.
examples: My grandfather went {bald} in his forties.
wrong: He is bald and has long, thick hair.

words.meaning: Describes hair that curves gently up and down.
examples: She has long, {wavy} brown hair.
wrong: Her wavy hair was completely straight.

words.meaning: Light in color, used about hair or skin.
examples: He has {fair} hair and blue eyes.
wrong: Her fair hair was jet black.

words.meaning: Describes hair that is pale yellow or golden.
examples: The {blond} girl is my cousin.
wrong: His blond hair was as dark as coal.

words.meaning: Small brown spots on the skin, often on the face.
examples: She has red hair and {freckles} on her nose.
wrong: Freckles are long hairs that grow on the chin.

words.meaning: Hair that grows above a man’s top lip.
examples: My uncle has a thick black {mustache}.
wrong: He grew a mustache on top of his head.

words.meaning: A small line in the skin that comes with age.
examples: My grandmother has {wrinkles} around her eyes.
wrong: The baby’s face was full of deep wrinkles from old age.

words.meaning: Having a nice face; attractive.
examples: The actor is very {good-looking}.
wrong: He’s so good-looking that nobody wants to look at him.

words.meaning: Very beautiful or attractive.
examples: She looked {gorgeous} in her wedding dress.
wrong: The view was gorgeous, so we turned away quickly.

words.meaning: Stylish and graceful in the way you look or move.
examples: She wore an {elegant} black dress to the party.
wrong: He looked elegant in his dirty, torn clothes.

words.meaning: Untidy and a bit dirty in the way you look.
examples: He came to work in {scruffy} old jeans.
wrong: He looked scruffy in his clean new suit.

words.meaning: Wearing nice, smart clothes.
examples: The guests at the wedding were all {well-dressed}.
wrong: He was well-dressed in a dirty old shirt with holes.

words.meaning: Hair tied together at the back of the head so it hangs down.
examples: She ties her hair in a {ponytail} when she runs.
wrong: He wears his ponytail on his feet.

words.meaning: Neither young nor old, about 45 to 65 years old.
examples: A {middle-aged} couple lives next door.
wrong: The middle-aged man was only six years old.

words.meaning: How tall a person or thing is.
examples: He is of average {height}.
wrong: We measured his height with a kitchen scale.

words.meaning: Having skin that is lighter than usual, often because you are ill.
examples: You look {pale}. Are you feeling sick?
wrong: She was pale because her face was bright red.

words.meaning: Having skin made darker by the sun.
examples: She came back from the beach very {tanned}.
wrong: He was tanned because he stayed inside all summer.

words.meaning: To look or behave like an older member of your family.
examples: She {takes after} her mother; they have the same smile.
wrong: He takes after his father, who is nothing like him.

words.meaning: To look like or be similar to someone or something.
examples: He strongly {resembles} his older brother.
wrong: The two sisters resemble each other because they look totally different.

words.meaning: The way someone or something looks.
examples: She cares a lot about her {appearance}.
wrong: His appearance is the sound of his voice.

words.meaning: The kind of person you are and how you behave.
examples: She has a warm, friendly {personality}.
wrong: Her personality is the color of her eyes.

words.meaning: The ability to find things funny and make others laugh.
examples: He has a great {sense of humor} and tells good jokes.
wrong: With his good sense of humor, he never laughs at anything.

words.meaning: Not telling the truth; likely to lie or cheat.
examples: The {dishonest} seller lied about the car.
wrong: He was dishonest, so he always told the truth.

words.meaning: Often angry or easily annoyed.
examples: He is always {bad-tempered} before breakfast.
wrong: She’s so bad-tempered that she never gets angry.

words.meaning: Not able to wait calmly; easily annoyed by delays.
examples: He gets {impatient} when the bus is late.
wrong: She is impatient and happy to wait for hours.

words.meaning: Enjoying meeting and spending time with other people.
examples: She’s very {sociable} and loves parties.
wrong: He is sociable, so he avoids people and stays alone.

words.meaning: Happy to listen to and accept new or different ideas.
examples: My grandmother is very {open-minded} about new music.
wrong: He is so open-minded that he refuses to hear new ideas.

words.meaning: Thinking you are better or more important than others.
examples: He became {big-headed} after he won the prize.
wrong: She is big-headed and thinks she is worse than everyone.

words.meaning: Not brave; too afraid to do what is right.
examples: It was {cowardly} of him to run away.
wrong: The cowardly soldier ran toward the danger to save his friend.

words.meaning: Moving in a careless way and often dropping or breaking things.
examples: I’m so {clumsy}; I dropped another glass.
wrong: She is clumsy, so she never drops or breaks anything.

words.meaning: Behaving like a younger person; not sensible for your age.
examples: It’s {immature} to laugh at someone who falls.
wrong: He was immature and acted very wisely for his age.

words.meaning: Not paying enough attention to what you do.
examples: A {careless} mistake cost him the exam.
wrong: He is careless and checks every detail twice.

words.meaning: Practical, honest and easy to talk to.
examples: Even though she’s famous, she is very {down-to-earth}.
wrong: He is down-to-earth and thinks he is better than everyone.

words.meaning: Liking to talk a lot.
examples: My little sister is very {talkative}.
wrong: He is talkative, so he hardly says a word.

words.meaning: Easily annoyed and in a bad mood.
examples: Dad is always {grumpy} when he is tired.
wrong: She was grumpy and smiled happily at everyone.

words.meaning: Often forgetting things because you are thinking about something else.
examples: My {absent-minded} uncle left his keys in the fridge.
wrong: He is absent-minded and never forgets anything.
